title: Title
notes: Open by emphasizing that correlation is not one reusable scalar once angles and spheres enter the data set. The chapter asks what a residual means on each sample space, which transformations should be ignored, and which null model preserves the observed directional margins.

title: Route
notes: Use this route slide as the organizing principle for the lecture. The same word, dependence, hides several different tasks: fit a linear height over a circle, compare two angles on a torus, rotate one sphere to another, or detect persistence in an ordered directional sequence.

title: Linear-Circular Model
notes: Pause on the cylinder before introducing the formula. The sine and cosine columns are not a trick for making angles linear; they are the coordinate representation of a circular predictor, and the fitted curve should be read as height varying around a closed loop.

title: Origin Invariance
notes: Make the invariance test operational. If an analyst can change the reported strength of line-circle dependence merely by relabeling north or midnight, the statistic is measuring the coordinate convention. The sine-cosine regression passes because the shift only rotates the predictor basis.

title: Circular-Circular Torus
notes: Introduce circular-circular association as a problem on the product space, not as a scatterplot with two troublesome axes. The torus picture explains why positive and negative rotational dependence are distinct alternatives and why residuals must be wrapped after fitting an offset.

title: Wrapped Residuals
notes: This slide is where residual geometry should become unavoidable. An ordinary subtraction can turn a small angular discrepancy into a jump near the cut point, while the wrapped residual preserves the torus relation and gives a meaningful concentration diagnostic.

title: Spherical-Spherical Correlation
notes: Do not let the trace formula feel like a black box. The covariance blocks summarize how centered coordinates in one sphere move with centered coordinates in the other, while the inverse blocks normalize the marginal scatter so the final scalar is not tied to a chosen coordinate frame.

title: Rotation Regression
notes: Frame regression as a constrained prediction problem. If the fitted value is supposed to be a direction, the model should not predict a point inside Euclidean space; a rotation keeps predictions on the sphere, and subtracting the radial component makes the residual tangent.

title: Model Map
notes: This is the conceptual bridge from correlation coefficients to modeling. The chapter includes bivariate model families, but the useful habit is to ask what the conditional object is, where the residual lives, and which transformations leave the scientific conclusion unchanged.

title: Directional Time Series
notes: The time-series example is a warning against unwrapping by habit. A persistent angular process should be detected through adjacent wrapped increments, and the null comparison should break ordering while preserving the observed sample of directions.

title: Permutation Nulls
notes: Emphasize that permutation is not just a convenient computation. In this chapter it is the way the analysis protects the circular or spherical margins while breaking only the relationship under study, giving a null distribution that answers the same geometric question as the statistic.

title: Noise Calibration
notes: Use the calibration lab to connect visual tightness with numerical dependence. As concentration increases, the torus band becomes narrower, the positive-rotation statistic increases, and the wrapped residual shrinks, so students see the statistic as a measurement of geometry rather than a magic number.

title: Diagnostic Residuals
notes: This slide turns the chapter into a reusable diagnostic checklist. Instead of asking whether a residual plot looks small in a flat chart, ask whether the residual was computed in the correct geometric space and whether its interpretation survives relabeling or rotation.

title: Notebook Contract
notes: Connect the deck back to the notebook without turning the lecture into a file tour. The important point is that each major visual has a machine-checkable invariant nearby, so the chapter teaches both statistical reasoning and implementation discipline.

title: Recap
notes: Close by asking students to make the four design choices before computing a correlation coefficient: sample space, statistic, null, and residual. The exercise reinforces the invariance theme, because a zero-direction relabeling should rotate coordinates without changing the reported strength of dependence.
